// default_engine: Model picker / CLI default when none specified. Prefer parakeet for English live; use sensevoice for Cantonese.
// parakeet_feed_sec: Audio seconds fed to Parakeet per add_audio (~0.3–0.5). Lower = snappier drafts, more thrash.
// post_final_cooldown_sec: Seconds the live engines discard mic audio after each committed final (cuts self-echo / reprint). 0 disables. Useful range about 0.8–1.5.
// post_stop_polish: After stopping live, re-decode the whole recorded session in one batch pass (full-utterance context, like a push-to-talk dictation app) and replace the transcript. Records raw mic audio during live. On speakers (no headphones) room echo lands in that recording — set false if polish output duplicates lines.
// mic_blocksize: sounddevice frames per callback at 16 kHz (~3200–4096 cuts Python wakeups; keep latency reasonable).
// vad_min_rms: Minimum mic energy (0–1) the live engines treat as speech. Higher = less sensitive to ambient / bleed.
// min_final_chars: Prefer not emitting tiny Parakeet finals shorter than this unless the delta ends in punctuation. Latency still wins over perfect segmentation.
// sample_rate: Engines contract. Fixed at 16000 Hz mono float32; other values are ignored.
// cooldown_ms: Same post-final window for the shared helper in engines/audio_util.py (default 1200, useful range 800–1500; 0 disables). Live engines read post_final_cooldown_sec.
// min_rms: prepare_chunk drops audio quieter than this when a caller does not pass its own gate. Kept low for soft speech; vad_min_rms is what the live engines pass.
// target_rms: Quiet speech is gained toward this RMS, capped at 4x so echo is not amplified.
// device_blocklist: Case-insensitive substrings. Loopbacks are never chosen when another input exists.
// device_prefer: Ordered name hints. First match among non-blocklisted inputs wins.
